analysis: Both changes are documentation only, with no code, config, or mode changes. In docs/architecture/security/encryption.md (head lines 121-122), a sentence is added: a delta checkpoint names its parent only through a keyed commitment, so files of one conversation stay unlinkable without the cache key. It replaces the 'are unchanged' wording about DBK3 metadata. This is a privacy claim about the T-041 leak #2 class: a disk observer testing guessed prefixes or linking files. It is consistent with T-041's posture (HMAC-keyed names, nothing prompt-derived beyond keyed tags in metadata). The underlying delta-checkpoint implementation and the DBK3 format reference (docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md) are not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify that the parent commitment is really keyed under K_lookup or the KEK, or that the file count, sizes, and mtimes do not still let an observer link a conversation chain. The claim 'unlinkable' may overstate this: residual metadata such as mtimes and sizes can still correlate files. The next pass should confirm this against the SSDBlockStore implementation and consider updating T-041's accepted-residual-metadata list to mention delta parent commitments and the new DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS flag, since T-041 detection_hint says nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added to metadata. docs/developer/test.md (head lines 673-675) only documents a benchmark report adding delta files and output tokens, plus an env var for a complete-file baseline. It introduces no new attack surface. No regression to the threat model is identified from the docs alone. The residual uncertainty is on the code side, which is not in this batch.
